advisory_notice: All SQA findings, rankings and assessments are recommendations. Master decides whether, when and how to act through docs/plan.json.
priority_assessment: I agree with master putting moss-close/run first. I would accept the close from the scorecard published for that run and generate the README from the same record (SQA-474). The latest local publication I found is for 5c9092545, before served-parts/clock. Its five numeric image rows already satisfy the shape the close looks for. Completed cells with valid credit can carry forward.

Of the rules I would remove, the verifier’s veto on shell assignments comes first (SQA-483). It stopped full-measurement/run after nine hours of measurement. The CUDA header line limit also stopped a MOSS repair (SQA-500). Moving that refusal earlier still requires a file split that preserves the compiled program. Master has now removed the nested-ternary veto. The shell parser, status-turn holds, sync.Once and comment punctuation already have plan steps.

I would settle which bytes a landing may publish before broadening reuse of checks (SQA-494). The remaining picture-selection defect can send a full draw to the wrong input (SQA-492). The filename veto on three test fakes (SQA-501) can go when master next touches the duplication check.

findings.input: Keep five numeric image rows in the store and an earlier published scorecard with a numeric MOSS row. Check moss-close/run before its closing cycle publishes. For recovery, start a second cycle at a commit with an earlier publication and let a required lane fail before the second cycle publishes.
findings.expected: Accept the campaign close and write its README from the same completed publication for the intended measurement commit and obligations. On a failed cycle, return the error and retain its completed cells for retry. The existing cycle and publication owners can supply that evidence to moss-close/run and own-record/do.
findings.actual: At 70394cb96 the close counts five image rows from a live store view. writeScorecard in display mode returns before reading HEAD or publishing. writeReadme independently selects the newest published record. The latest retained publication, 5c9092545, already has numeric times for all five models, and the committed README shows MOSS at 65.3 s. Neither check binds those data to the closing cycle. On same-commit recovery, improvement.Measure can return another cycle’s record after a lane error, then Improve calls Fill and clears the retry state. Both acceptance failures follow from source. No premature campaign close or loss of retry state was observed.

findings.input: Give the plan the original full-measurement/run check from 5147c611f's parent. It saves the scorecard output in a shell variable and then checks each required model row and the generated README.
findings.expected: Remove the assignment-only refusal for a verifier that captures a command’s output and asserts on it. Use the shell’s exit status for the composite command and keep the existing checks for missing tests and unproven cache credit. check-form-reads/do already owns this. An absent model row must still fail the verifier.
findings.actual: Git Bash accepted the exact recorded command in syntax-only mode. ParseVerify splits at the opening parenthesis, consumes the assignment prefix and reports that the segment runs nothing. The landing refusal and commit 8e62553db record that this stopped full-measurement/run after nine hours of measurement. Commit 5147c611f rewrote the check before the step landed. The filing check now gives the same refusal earlier. The nine hours elapsed before the refusal. The record shows a verifier rewrite and a separate landing.

findings.input: Start the landing fixture with unformatted internal/p/p.go. After gofmt writes it and recordWrites records that path, append a separate, valid function for the next step to the same file before fix calls shipSet. The first step’s assertion on the original function still passes.
findings.expected: Publish only the first candidate and the gate’s edits to those bytes. Leave the later function in the checkout for its own step. Use the existing candidate or keep the exact output of the transformation. The snapshot fixture can distinguish both copies with this same-file edit.
findings.actual: b9bac4955 protects other paths, including later.go and notes.txt in the existing fixture. recordWrites keeps a boolean for p.go after comparing its hashes. A later capture starts at the first tree but stages the current checkout bytes of every gateWrote path, including the later function in p.go. The earlier cross-step landing was observed at b1d6e237a. This remaining case was established from source at 70394cb96.

findings.input: In the composer's MOSS image-to-image mode, open two stored PNG output cards, A and B, and use each as input for the same picture slot, A first. Let B's content request return first, then A's. Submit after both return.
findings.expected: Select B by its stored output ID and declared image type when its button is clicked. The picture slot needs no blob fetch to set that value. Keep the existing file download for the attachment path that actually consumes bytes. Extend the generated-media browser case to inspect the submitted ID after the two clicks.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at cb82910a6. The gallery supplies each card's artifact ID and MIME type. mediaCard waits for api.blob, constructs a File and calls reuse. The slot branch in chat.js uses the file type to choose the field, then assigns the ID. B is selected first and A overwrites it when the older fetch returns. Request.ReadPictures now accepts both output IDs, so the model can draw from A. The retained single-card check verifies one slot assignment. The two-click failure was not observed in a run.

findings.input: In MOSS depth control, request the preview for picture A. While that response is pending, choose B and then A again. Let A's response display its map. Select B once more without requesting another preview.
findings.expected: On the last selection of B, clear A's map. Associate a displayed response with its picture and settings using the existing showing value, or discard a response once its original selection was invalidated. Keep preview generation on the button press. The held-response case can exercise this sequence with one estimate.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at cb82910a6. Selecting B clears showing. Returning to A leaves showing null. A's response passes madeFrom() === asked and inserts the image without restoring showing. The last switch to B cannot clear the map because offer requires showing !== null. The existing browser case covers changing away once and clearing an already displayed map. This return-to-A sequence was not run.

findings.input: After a passing needle-reference run, delete only fixtures/needle_upstream_calls.json and select lanes with -reached. The reader still names the old path. The same case applies to the models lane when only fixtures/moss/checkpoint.json is deleted.
findings.expected: CycleLanesReached selects the reader of the removed fixture, so the Needle or MOSS check reports the missing input. Use the existing reader lookup for deleted paths, or run the lane when its readers are unknown. Keep the current package selection for edits to existing fixtures.
findings.actual: Source trace at c71a1e230. The Git diff supplies the deleted path. TrackedDocuments lists only files still present, so documentReaders returns no entry. discover treats the missing entry as zero readers and omits the lane. Both checks fail on the missing file if selected. The retained gate verified selection for edits to both fixtures while they were present.

findings.input: Record two different PNGs returned by node 449 with the same basename original.png in subfolders MOSS/a and MOSS-a of the same recording.
findings.expected: Keep each output under a distinct name and leave both recorded hashes verifiable. The recorder already computes the content hash and its existing two-output case can check both names and bytes.

findings.input: The owner tells the lead to pause the campaign. Before the lead records the requested stop, a second session in the same checkout asks for progress. The lead still owns the worktree and has the same stop request.
findings.expected: Honor the owner's explicit request in the session that received it. Remove the rule that the most recent prompt anywhere in the checkout must contain a stop word. Keep the existing scoped stop record and explicit owner authorization. A progress request in a different chat should neither grant nor revoke that authorization.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at 30691fc67. runPrompt calls NoteStopRequest before checking who holds the worktree or whether the session is a reviewer. Both sessions write or remove the same stop_request file. The progress question removes it, so RequireStopRequest refuses the lead's authorized pause before RecordStop. Conversely, the word test accepts “don't stop” as evidence for a later requested pause. The words alone never pause a run. The existing checks exercise successive prompts in one session. No missed or unauthorized pause was observed in this review.

findings.input: Master starts a typed status-only turn in a clean checkout with an open plan. Before it answers, SQA edits only docs/sqa_findings.json. Master has made no edit. No landing, recorded stop or policy decision is pending.
findings.expected: Let master finish its answer. Exclude the findings register from the stop hook's abandoned-work check alongside the plan, using plan.FindingsRegister. The next implementation landing already carries both files. Extend the existing plan_rides case so that a register edit alone passes and a source edit beside it still blocks.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at b1d6e237a. turnCreatedDirt compares checkout snapshots and exempts only plan.Path. The new register edit therefore makes stopDecision return stopOrphan. On its first stop the hook exits 2 and tells master to land or revert the reviewer's work. An unchanged retry can pass. commitScope explicitly includes the register in the next landing. This review did not observe a blocked session.

findings.input: In the implementing chat, ask for a status answer only and explicitly end the turn there. The checkout is clean, no landing is running, and the only remaining row needs the lead's decision about a standing rule. The campaign itself has no recorded pause.
findings.expected: Let the lead answer the question and end that turn. Keep the pending decision visible for the next implementation turn. Dispatch and landing already hold the affected row until the lead answers. Remove the requirement to decide unrelated policy before returning a status answer. Ordinary implementation turns should still take the authorized decision without waiting for the owner.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at db04fec59. stopDecision permits the clean, typed turn to end. Before using that verdict, runStop calls answerHold. A nonempty Dispatch.Answer makes the hook return exit 2 and tell the lead to answer the decision now. The unchanged-state retry can subsequently let the turn end. The eight-hour capacity-record-history wait recorded in 528f40b3f preceded this hook change. The current refusal follows from the call order and the existing owner-turn cases. No repeat of the eight-hour wait was observed.

findings.input: Give Unwrap the first comment line “Unwrap returns fs.ErrNotExist.” Add a blank line and an indented Go example whose last line is errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist). The comment ends with the closing parenthesis of the call.
findings.expected: Remove the name-and-terminal-period test as a reason to refuse a landing. Keep documentation of the error contract and let review judge its wording. The usage example should remain valid Go as printed. A punctuation change should have no bearing on acceptance of the method.

The documented example fails, while the same method with only its first sentence passes. Eight retained rules refusals name export-doc, including served-answers/absent for Error and Unwrap. The count establishes that the rule blocked landings. The example is source-demonstrated and the logs do not identify it as the cause of all eight.

findings.input: A serving or training observation published by servingattempt.Record or trainingworkflow.Observer.finish when (a) the recipe-state read fails and the incoming Verification is empty, or (b) the same recipe is activated again, verified, after the recorded attempt executed it not verified.
findings.expected: Publication carries the state the executed recipe and task had at execution. A failed state read is told apart from a historical absent state and earns no verified credit, and a later activation does not replace execution-time state. Legacy bytes, the own-verifying-run exception and partial or cancelled results keep their contract.
findings.actual: The two remaining owners still read state at publication and drop the lookup error: servingattempt.Record (servingattempt.go:117-119) and Observer.finish (session_observation.go:271-273). A failed read leaves an empty Verification; scorecard.unverifiedAside rejects only explicit not-verified/broken and accepts that empty value as legacy. A later same-recipe activation is written as the attempt's state in place of its execution-time not-verified state. Shown from source at 8acbf71d17dfd3e1e35313b370f900b21f0fdf10; no SQA execution.

findings.input: (3) Gemma accuracy over 32 independent media, each with two uniformly guessed 3-choice questions. (4) Two judges ranked on all-constant finite scores, and on probabilities (.9,.1) against (.45,.45). (6) Two GIF media inputs for their own bound renders, with one judge and scorer, decoded at 16 frames against 1. (7) The embedded SenseNova APG verdict edited to 0 wins, 524 losses, 0 ties, 80 media and tail 0.0001, Admitted left true, with Says changed consistently to 'admitted: a gain beyond chance, 0 wins, 524 losses and 0 ties over 80 media'; its evaluation IDs stay unchanged. (8) A render campaign resumed after an earlier item's request changed while its last item drew the same, or with truncated bookkeeping.
findings.expected: (3) The accuracy null matches the actual choice counts and within-media dependence. (4) Ranking uses the aggregation production scores with, and an undefined tau or omitted resamples are said, without a panic. (6) A reading is admitted only from evaluations bound to the same render, decode sampling and question contract, and a control offers a candidate only by the admission for its own model, recipe and request. (7) The record's verdict, counts and tail are derived through AdmitPreset and its bound evaluations, so drift is refused. (8) A completed arm or verdict is reused only for the same bound inputs, evaluator and producer; changed work is refused or redone, and truncated bookkeeping does not count as complete.
findings.actual: (3) Correct count minus sum(1/choices) against zero is taken as a fair sign for ExactPairedBinary: a medium is positive with probability 5/9, and uniform guessing passes the 22-positive threshold (nominal tail 0.0250512) with probability 0.0914273, above the 0.05 level. (4) Arithmetic probability means rank (.9,.1) above (.45,.45), the reverse of production softShare's geometric mean; constant scores give a NaN tau, all 2000 resamples are dropped and resampledTau indexes an empty slice. (6) judgedRender compares content, request, producer, runtime and scorer but not MediaInput.Decode or the question contract, readRender never calls verifyRendered, ResolveActiveExecution takes the current activation, and the embedded offering uses recorded no-loss flags (plus a recorded gain for guidance methods) under a published model name/preset key, without runtime recipe/request binding. (7) The native record test checks evaluation-ID syntax, displayed counts and admitted/refused wording, but does not recompute Admitted or Tail through AdmitPreset and the bound evaluations. Gained trusts Tail <= falseGain, so the consistently worded false gain in input 7 passes the record and gain checks and offers APG on SenseNova's page despite its stated 524 losses and zero wins. (8) Arm, suite and verdict skips trust names and file existence and accept truncated bookkeeping, and a new build is validated by re-rendering only the last item. Remaining counterexamples shown from source and arithmetic at 0c24aca5b670940f95c0f8156c13804a9e2fd9ea; no SQA execution.

findings.input: A retained ClipMotion observation of unchanged MP4 bytes, then a motion encoder checkpoint or FFmpeg/preprocessing configuration changes under the same encoder basename. The suite is compiled again with that old observation and the same matching clip-content digest.
findings.expected: Motion readings identify the encoder/checkpoint and decoder/sampling contract that produced them, so changed instruments cannot silently reuse or be credited with an old metric. Keep the repaired OCR re-keying, content checks and whole-set exclusion in the existing media compiler and observation producers; the observation instrument is separate from the answering judge.
findings.actual: The remaining motion instrument is not bound: writeMotion passes filepath.Base(encoderPath) to measureMotion; ClipMotion stores that Encoder string and clip/source content digests, with no encoder/checkpoint or FFmpeg/sampling identity. ClipMotion.validate requires only a nonempty encoder name, and bindObservations compares clip.Content alone before keeping the motion set. Changing an instrument while the clip bytes and encoder basename stay the same therefore leaves the old motion admissible and its actual producing instrument indistinguishable. Shown from source at ba0405e63d92653b84f617d8c332d5546529e444; no SQA execution.
